research_question: How well does the unchanged official EqMotion architecture learn each Tartan airport from that airport's registered training dates only?

grid.coordinate_frame: local east,north,up km; per-airport fixed reference

model.registered_heads: first five heads fixed before formal training
model.probabilities: uniform 0.2 over the five registered candidates
model.top1_decision: fixed candidate 0 solely to satisfy the shared evaluator interface

training.checkpoint_policy: fixed final epoch 20; development metrics are diagnostic and never select a checkpoint
training.development_evaluation: once after loading the fixed final checkpoint
training.seed_expansion_gate: This v1 protocol registers seed 42 only. Any multi-seed expansion requires a new result-free frozen protocol after both airport seed-42 runs complete.

evaluation.probability_policy: Uniform probabilities define an empirical finite measure, so Energy is comparable under the matched K=5 protocol.
evaluation.top1_limitation: EqMotion's registered diverse heads have no learned categorical ranking. Fixed candidate 0 is arbitrary; Top-1, NLL, Brier, ECE, and rank metrics are not publication-comparable and are omitted from results.

test_lock.policy: This runner has no test split argument and must not resolve, construct, cache, or evaluate either locked test dataset.

execution.prerequisite: Run only after the current risk-head GPU wave has released cuda:0. Each command creates a new directory and refuses to overwrite it.
execution.batch_size_evidence: Matched EqMotion local throughput gate at batch 512 used 842604032 peak GPU bytes; target-domain ASCENT-family frozen batches are 256 train / 512 evaluation. EqMotion uses 512 for both to avoid changing optimizer-step count by airport-specific tuning.
execution.formal_order: KAGC seed42 then KBTP seed42 on the single GPU; do not run them concurrently.

claim_boundary: Target-only EqMotion development results are a modern strong-baseline check on the frozen retrospective Tartan date split. Only K=5 minADE, minFDE, Energy, and efficiency are comparable; no probability calibration or Top-1 claim is supported.
